results.title: Electronics Manufacturing Services for 2026 Tariff Mitigation
results.content:
Check the country of origin and classification of imported products carefully. Tariffs differ between bare printed circuit boards and PCBAs, so any errors in classification could be costly. Country of origin is important because moving certain assembly steps outside of China can legally change the product’s origin and reduce tariff exposure. [...] China, which manufactures more than 50% of the world’s printed circuit boards, has been particularly affected by the tariffs. Plans were finalized for semiconductor tariffs to rise to 50% under the China review. This measure is aimed at chips, but it pulls through costs into many electronic assemblies that sit on PCBs. Additionally, the USTR extended some expiring exclusions into 2026. Many categories lost their exclusions, including some printed circuit board assemblies, which means those [...] ### The Direct Impacts of Tariffs on PCBA Prices

When it comes to tariffs, bare PCBs are classified differently than printed circuit board assemblies. Because of this, they face different tariff rules. If a tariff exemption on PCBAs expires, companies may suddenly have to pay the full tariff rate again. Making sure PCBAs are classified correctly and the country of origin is properly documented can make a big difference in final costs for your company.

results.title: New Electronic Component Tariffs: How to Prevent Supply ...
results.content: Rising raw material costs and increased tariffs on Chinese imports are driving up prices across the electronics and renewable energy sectors. The U.S. relies heavily on China for rare earth elements like helium and neodymium dysprosium, which are essential for electric vehicle motors and wind turbines, as well as indium, which significantly raises the cost of LCDs and solar panels. Additionally, tariffs on Chinese-made electronic components – such as printed circuit boards (PCBs), [...] Country/Region of Origin and Supply Chain Intelligence (SCI) data in Accuris Electronic Parts Solutions offer visibility into part sources – including those from China – helping businesses categorize components as high, medium, or low risk based on their impact on supply chains. U.S. tariff data, which will be incorporated in the Accuris solutions soon, will offer visibility into the tariff-impacted components. [...] especially if China dominates production. Some companies may push for domestic sourcing based on the incentives provided under the CHIPS Act, but this could be expensive due to higher U.S. labor and production costs. Preparing for these potential tariffs will be part of a successful strategy for U.S.-based manufacturers.

results.title: How Tariffs Are Affecting the PCB Circuit Board Industry
results.content: China — the largest producer of PCBs in the world — has been the primary target of the administration’s tariffs. As such, imported goods from China currently face the highest country-specific tariff rates of any nation in the world, with the average imported good facing a 30% tariff at the very least. However, even this lowered tariff rate may not last, as it is the result of a 90-day trade agreement between the U.S. and China. [...] As such, each business relying on PCBs will need to evaluate its own supply chain to determine the specific effect of tariffs on its import prices. Even if your business is not importing fully functional PCBs from China or Mexico, you may still have to deal with increased prices on copper, semiconductors and other PCB components. The import price may be lower overall, but it will still be increased by the universal 10% tariff at a bare minimum. [...] Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are the backbone of most technology on the planet. They power everything from smartphones and machine learning algorithms to microwaves and air fryers. While many of the tech companies that work with and rely on these PCBs are based in the United States, most of the PCBs themselves are manufactured overseas in countries like China, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea.
